title: Standby Swarm Simulation Orchestrator for Private VPC DR validation
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build an orchestrator that can instantiate a configurable "standby swarm" across multiple customer VPC regions and run non-disruptive and disruptive DR validation scenarios. The goal is to automate lifecycle of ephemeral standby clusters, exercise lease-based cluster arbitration, KV-prefetch and fencing, routing siphon assertions, and post-swap SLO scans without requiring manual cutovers. This ticket covers Terraform modules, orchestration state machine, health checks, and a smoke-run harness hooked into our console dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform modules to create ephemeral standby clusters per-region with single CLI flag (module inputs documented)
Orchestrator can run a role-swap simulation that promotes a standby to primary without changing DNS (traffic siphon via proxy rules)
Health checks include: KV sync validation, in-memory KV-cache warming, model-compatibility probe, request-path latency histogram, and end-to-end SLO assertion (p99 <= configured target)
Automated rollbacks implemented for failed promotion attempts with deterministic fencing (lease revoke + KV lock cleanup)
End-to-end test run appears in Console runbook dashboard with links to Grafana panels and generated run artifact (tarball of logs + tracer spans)
No customer-facing primary is accidentally modified during simulation (test accounts and isolated routing only)
Documentation and runbook (Confluence) updated with run steps, runbook checklist, and troubleshooting playbacks
technical_notes: Orchestrator is a small state machine service (go) that drives Terraform via the existing infra-deployer library; will use stateful step markers in S3 for idempotency
Use lease-based arbitration: leader lease stored in KV with TTL; standby attempts promotion only when lease expired and fences competing candidates
Traffic siphon pattern: envoy proxy config on standby to mirror and siphon a terminated percentage using header rewrite; avoids DNS changes for real traffic tests
KV preflight: snapshot compare between primary and standby using prefix hashes; failure threshold configurable
Health probes: model warmup + token-throughput microbench; synthetic inference workload generator bundled in harness
Terraform modules: outputs must include cluster_id, service_ips, proxy_config, and kv_prefix artifact to feed orchestration
Audit: every step emits structured events to our observability pipeline tagged run_id, region, scenario, and step
